title: Impact Pathways and Internal Systems Handbook
author: Asha Patel
content:
Overview

Purpose: This handbook codifies how Redwood turns individual contributor growth goals into predictable role ladders and tool access pathways. It ties career ladders to concrete operational systems (onboarding automation, identity & access flows, benefits allocations), so people-ops, managers, and engineers can make consistent decisions.

Audience: managers, ICs, people-ops partners, hiring leads, and platform engineers who maintain onboarding and access tooling.

Scope: working-at-Redwood practices, role ladder checkpoints, benefits alignment, and the internal tools + processes that gate access and enable career progress.

Principles (short):
- Transparency: role criteria and tooling gates are documented and discoverable.
- Predictability: a defined pathway reduces ad hoc promotions and slows drift.
- Developer-first tooling: onboarding and access are automated where possible.
- Inclusive mobility: lateral moves and skills sprints are first-class.

1) Role Ladders and Competency Mapping

Summary: Role ladders are organized as three lenses: scope, complexity, and enablement. Each role level includes a skills passport, measurable outcomes, and a recommended set of tools/permissions required to operate at that level.

Key components: 
- Skills Passport: brief checklist of competencies (technical design, cross-team impact, mentoring, operational ownership).
- Outcome Examples: concrete, time-bounded deliverables used in calibration.
- Tooling Profile: the set of internal systems (e.g., Redwood Console - full read/write, Grafana Dashboards - view-only or edit, CI/CD staging deployer, billing view) mapped to each level.

Sample ladder row (template):

| Level | Scope (team/org) | Core Outcomes (90d) | Tools & Permissions | Sample Promotion Evidence |
|-------|------------------|----------------------|---------------------|--------------------------|
| IC2   | Single repo/component | Lead a small feature, ship 1 A/B test | Console: read, CI: write for feature branches | PRs, peer feedback, metrics |
| IC3   | Multi-service ownership | Lead cross-team launch, mentor 1-2 ICs | Console: write, Grafana edit, Staging deploy | Launch report, design review notes |

How promotions are initiated: 
1. Employee or manager files an internal promotion request in the PeopleOps portal (use flow: /people-ops/promote).
2. Employee uploads evidence mapped to the template (PR links, metrics, feedback).
3. People-ops schedules calibration — manager, peer reviewer, and an org-level reviewer review.
4. Decision communicated within two weeks; updates written to the role profile and entitlement system.

2) Onboarding and First 90 Days (Systems + Checklists)

Goal: Make the first 90 days predictable and time-to-impact fast. This section lists automated steps the joiner and manager use, and the toolchain that owns each step.

Automated onboarding flow (owner/tool):
- Account provisioning: Okta SSO + SCIM (Identity team)
- Workstation build: machine-image via FleetOps (infra)
- Access artifacts: RBAC roles applied using AccessBot (people-ops + eng-platform)
- Internal orientation: automated invites to Welcome cohort (Calendar + Docs)
- First-week projects: templated Git repo (internal-starters) + README tasks

First-week checklist (manager):
1. Confirm Okta login and MFA.
2. Confirm machine assigned and dev container image runs.
3. Pair the teammate with an onboarding buddy and schedule 1:1s.
4. Ensure employee has Console read access and can view team dashboards.
5. Walk through benefits enrollment links (PeopleOps portal).

90-day goals template (to be completed by manager + IC):
- 30d: Setup and small shipping task completed with PR reviews.
- 60d: Ship first cross-repo change or contribute to a product area metric.
- 90d: Lead a retro and document a runbook/update OWNERS.

3) Internal Tools and Access Policies

Canonical tools referenced in this handbook:
- Redwood Console (console.redwood.internal) — model for product metrics, usage, and rollout controls.
- AccessBot — automated RBAC engine that maps role ladder to permissions.
- FleetOps — machine images, provisioning, and hardware assignment.
- Onboarder CLI — new-joiner helper (see samples).
- PeopleOps portal — cases for promotions, benefits, and role-change requests.

Access model rules:
- Principle of least privilege by default; role-based profiles grant base-level access.
- Elevated entitlements (deploy, billing-admin) require a manager-approved request and a 14-day review window.
- Tooling profiles are versioned; changes must pass a two-week review and be published by people-ops.

Sample AccessBot policy (YAML example):

# role-profile: IC3
permissions:
  - resource: console.projects
    actions: [read, write]
  - resource: grafana.team-dashboards
    actions: [read, edit]
  - resource: ci.subsystem
    actions: [create-branch, merge-to-staging]

CLI snippet: how to request elevated access

# Request deploy access via Onboarder
onboarder request access --resource ci.deploy --reason "lead release for payment service" --manager "jane.doe@redwood.com"

4) Benefits Allocation & Perks Mapping

How benefits tie to role level: many benefits are consistent across the company (healthcare, 401k match, flexible PTO), while other perks depend on role or tenure (hardware allowance, home office stipend, relocation). This section shows the simplified mapping and the process for exceptions.

Benefits mapping table (abridged):

| Benefit | Eligibility | Applied by | Notes |
|--------|-------------|-----------|-------|
| Home office stipend | All full-time after 1st paycheck | PeopleOps | One-time, expense submission via Concur |
| Hardware allowance | IC3+ or manager | Finance approvals | Requires manager sign-off and asset tagging |
| Relocation | New hires meeting role criteria | PeopleOps + Recruiting | One-time; review for approval within 10 business days |

Exception process: manager opens PeopleOps case with business justification, attaches promotion or role-change docs, PeopleOps and Finance respond within 7 business days.

5) Career Mobility Programs and Lateral Moves

Programs available:
- Skills Sprints: 6-week cohort-led programs for product, infra, and data engineering skill building.
- Rotation Fellowship: 3-month rotations across teams for cross-functional learning.
- Internal hiring referral for current employees: standard internal-applicant flow with interview guidance.

Lateral move steps (employee-initiated):
1. Discuss intent with current manager; get alignment on timing.
2. Submit lateral intent in PeopleOps portal and select target team.
3. Talent partner coordinates interviews and shared calibration.
4. If accepted, people-ops runs offboarding/onboarding steps, including entitlement handover.

6) Operational Playbooks (examples)

Onboarding failure recovery (quick):
1. New joiner cannot log in to console.redwood.internal.
2. Manager confirms Okta account exists.
3. If Okta exists but login fails, escalate to Identity team via #identity-support with joiner email and Okta trace id.
4. Identity team fixes SCIM sync issue and confirms via a Slack thread; manager marks step complete.

Promotion dispute triage (quick):
1. Employee appeals a promotion decision by opening a PeopleOps ticket with additional evidence.
2. PeopleOps convenes a re-calibration panel within 10 business days.
3. Panel includes original reviewers plus an org-level reviewer.
4. Final decision and remediation options are communicated by PeopleOps.

7) Ownership, SLAs, and Escalations

Ownership:
- PeopleOps: maintain role definitions, promotion process, benefits mapping, and onboarding flow templates.
- Eng-Platform: maintain AccessBot, Onboarder CLI, and FleetOps images.
- Identity team: Okta/SCIM and SSO integrations.

Service SLAs:
- Okta account provisioning: 24 hours from hire confirmation.
- Hardware provisioning: 5 business days (standard); expedite flow available with manager approval.
- Promotion decisions: 14 calendar days standard turnaround.

Escalation path:
1. Manager -> PeopleOps case -> (if not resolved) Director of PeopleOps -> CTO/Head of Eng if cross-org impact.

Appendices

A. Useful links and templates:
- PeopleOps portal: https://peopleops.internal.redwood/
- Onboarder CLI docs: internal-staff/docs/onboarder-cli.md
- Promotion evidence template: internal-staff/templates/promotion-evidence.md

B. FAQ (short)
Q: Who initiates benefits enrollment?
A: The manager sends the enrollment packet in the first-week checklist; employees complete enrollment in PeopleOps within 30 days to avoid coverage gaps.

Q: How do I get staging deploy access?
A: Submit an AccessBot request via Onboarder (see CLI snippet) and include a manager approver. The review window is 14 days.

C. Change log (summary)
